rulings.restated: Input — The asset class of this property: find the property in Pub. 946 Appendix B, Table B-1, and the activity it is used in in Table B-2 (use the Table B-2 class when the property is specifically listed there under your activity); or choose A (personal property with no class life), B (qualified technological equipment), C (property used in research and experimentation), or qualified improvement property
rulings.model: The IRS column (a) is 'Classification of property' and says to sort the property 'according to its classification (3-year property, 5-year property, etc.)'; the restatement instead asks for the Appendix B asset class or A/B/C/QIP.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation — the line is an intermediate in the project's basis computation. (a) the class input derives the form's 3/5/7-year classification through the Appendix B class; (b) the year plus the 2025 quarter gives the MACRS convention the form's month would give; (c) the pre-section-179 basis is shown under the column marker (c), and the form's column (c) after section 179 and the special allowance is item 19(c) (asset.col19c), which subtracts them. No printed tax amount differs. Lines 25 and 26(i) copy the per-asset allowance and elected cost, not the other lines' columns.

rulings.restated: Input — The year you placed this property in service in the business (2005 to 2025)
rulings.model: The IRS column (b) calls for the 'Month and year placed in service' and line 19 is only for assets placed in service during 2025, while the restatement asks only for the year and permits 2005 through 2025.

rulings.restated: Divide helper "The business use percentage, as cents" by helper "One hundred cents (100%)", rounded to 6 decimal places; if the result is 1 or more, use 1 (and 0 if it is less than 0). Multiply helper "Cost or other basis" by the result.
rulings.model: IRS line 19 column (c) says after multiplying cost by business use, 'subtract any credits and deductions allocable to the property' (including section 179 and the special allowance); the restatement stops after the multiplication.

rulings.restated: Choose — [helper "Special depreciation allowance for this class of property" = 'full' → helper "The allowance when it is claimed: 100% if acquired after January 19, 2025, otherwise 40%"] [helper "Special depreciation allowance for this class of property" = 'forty' → helper "40% special allowance"] [helper "Special depreciation allowance for this class of property" = 'none' → helper "Zero"]
rulings.model: The IRS also provides a 50% allowance for qualified reuse and recycling property and limits the 40% rate to property acquired after September 27, 2017; the restatement applies 40% to any property not acquired after January 19, 2025.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: finding — i4562 pp. 5–7, Line 14. The 40% rate applies to property acquired after September 27, 2017 and before January 20, 2025; qualified reuse and recycling property placed in service after August 31, 2008 is eligible for 50%. The restatement's "otherwise 40%" applies 40% to any property not acquired after January 19, 2025, and the bonus-choice question has no 50% branch. A pre-September-27-2017 asset can be given 40% and a reuse/recycling asset cannot be given 50%. BUG-0291; fix the screen and add the branches with the asset pass (T-158).

rulings.restated: Enter the amount from helper "Basis for MACRS depreciation (after section 179 and the special allowance)".
rulings.model: IRS line 19(c) says to subtract 'any credits and deductions allocable to the property'; the restatement subtracts only section 179 and the special allowance.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope — asset.screen refuses an asset whose basis was adjusted for anything other than depreciation (i4562 pp. 11–12), which covers the credits and deductions allocable to the property that column (c) subtracts. The MACRS basis subtracts section 179 and the special allowance, the two adjustments in this slice.

rulings.model: IRS line 25 says 'Enter on line 25 your total special depreciation allowance for all qualified listed property'; it is not the line 14 amount, which the restatement reports only for property other than listed property.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation — i4562 p. 13, Line 25. asset.f25 copies asset.bonus, the per-asset special allowance; the printed line 14 is the non-listed-property line, so "from line 14" is loose wording, not the value. The line is shown only for listed property placed in service in 2025, and the Schedule C totals read the per-asset amount filtered by asset.listed.

rulings.model: IRS line 25 says 'Enter on line 25 your total special depreciation allowance for all qualified listed property'; the restatement instead takes the line 14 amount, which is for non-listed property.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; restatement accepted. Line 14 and line 19 amounts are figured per asset and shown by listed status (asset.on_19, asset.on_26_2025); for listed property the same per-asset allowance, election and depreciation appear on lines 25, 26(i) and 26(h), figured by the line 19 instructions as i4562 p. 15, Column (h) directs. The objection reads the shared helper names as the other lines' columns.

rulings.restated: Add helper "MACRS on 2025 property" and helper "MACRS on property placed in service before 2025".
rulings.model: IRS line 26(h) says for property used more than 50% in a qualified business use and placed in service after 1986, 'figure column (h) by following the instructions for line 19, column (g)'; the restatement adds line 19(g)/line 17 amounts, which are for non-listed property, instead of computing from the listed property's own basis after line 26(i) and line 25.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation — i4562 p. 5, Line 6, and p. 16, Column (i). asset.f26i copies asset.s179, the per-asset elected section 179 cost; the printed line 6(c) is the non-listed-property column, so "from line 6(c)" is loose wording. A listed property's elected cost is the amount the 26(i) column asks for.
